qa#1 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYpxQpmErd1ixfkgbYh

Filed by the seat from the runner's report (runner session `session_01QSeKYmdkb7AqWcakxhcCpY`); the runner made no GitHub write.

## Environment fingerprint
- Framework `objectstack-ai/objectstack` 6091b645fd5a88f4e26b032261dc7bfd94b48f94 (#34565, `origin/main` at 10:54Z). `ui/` is in the same tree. CLI 18.5.0, Node v22.23.4, pnpm 10.31.0, 4 CPUs, 15.7 GiB.
- The clone was shallow, so I deepened it by 600 commits to reach b914e724. `b914e724..HEAD` is 393 commits.
- Build steps:
  - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
  - `pnpm build --concurrency=2` with `OS_SKIP_DTS` unset: 119 tasks, 0 cached, 15m32s.
  - `pnpm console:build --concurrency=2`: 11m50s.
  - `check-dev-prereqs`: 107/107.
- App: the stock showcase, booted per item as `objectstack dev --no-compile --no-watch --ui --seed-admin -p PORT -d file:/tmp/qa/GROUP/ITEM/data.db`, with `OS_PORT` and `OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT` exported. Each runner group had its own port range in 41300–41340.
- Isolation:
  - Package installs, CLI writes, self-pinging connectors and walled boots ran on scratch app copies with a private `OS_HOME`.
  - The showcase artifact `dist/objectstack.json` was unchanged throughout (md5 403a7a7e…). `.objectstack/installed-packages/` stayed absent and `git status` is clean.
  - `examples/app-showcase/.objectstack/data/` exists from the tree boots; RUNNER documents this as harmless.
- Personas:
  - `--seed-admin`, the seeded demo personas, invite-plus-sign-up members, and `admin/create-user` personas.
  - `qa-fixture walled-boot` for the second-organization legs.
  - Each persona's identity was proven server-side with `get-session`.
- Execution: parallel. Four live-runner subagents covered the Tier 2 and Tier 3 groups, 13 groups in all. Three scorer subagents scored the Tier 1 pins. All were opus at effort high.
  - Live runner groups (A1, A2, A2b, A2c, A2d, B1, B1b, B1c, B1d, M1, M1b, M1c, M1d, M2, M3) drove their clauses against live boots.
  - The three scorers (S1, S2, S3) scored Tier 1 clauses from pin output at the layer each pin reaches (RUNNER rule 6). They ran no tests themselves.
  - I ran the pins centrally in two streams: unit batches one package at a time with `--maxWorkers=1`, and dogfood one file per invocation.
- Timing (UTC): setup 10:54–11:23 (29 min); test 11:21–13:38 (2 h 17 min).

## Scope
- Selector `touched:b914e724`, resolved with `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs touched:b914e724 --json` at 6091b645.
  - 2489 files changed. 305 runnable items: 124 api, 102 mixed, 57 browser, 18 cli, 4 build. 8 blocked items are hidden.
  - No `planned` item matched.
  - Every revision scored equals the resolver's revision.
- Tiers:
  - **Tier 1: 165 items with `automated.ref`.** 558 pin test files were collected (499 named in refs, plus 59 sibling files my ref parser first missed and I re-ran). 16,246 tests passed and 1 failed.
    - The failure was `dogfood package-first-authoring` › "clones ACTIVE items…": "Test timed out in 5000ms" (5242 ms) under load. Two isolated re-runs gave 5/5 and 5/5, so it was environmental. It scores no clause.
    - The 11 `ui/e2e/live` Playwright specs were not run. Three items rest only on them (`records-forms.conditional-rules-grid`, `records-forms.adhoc-filter-sort-builder`, `attachments-storage.inline-grid-receipt-cells`); those were driven by hand in the browser instead (RUNNER objectui-path option (a)).
  - **Tier 2: 83 unpinned P0/P1 items.** 81 were driven live. The 2 not re-judged are carried forward.
  - **Tier 3: 57 P2 items.** 56 were driven live. The 1 not re-judged is carried forward.
- Clause tallies below read pass / partial / fail / blocked / not-run, then `s` for skipped or not applicable. "see runner tally" means the runner grouped several clauses on one line and my parser could not split them; the verdict is the derived one.

## FAIL rows: reproduction rules
**platform-core.app-management-toggle · rev 3 · acceptance[5] and negative[0] · fail.** Reproduced twice on fresh loads (12:59 and 13:05 UTC) with role-named clicks, and the network trace shows the order of the two writes.
1. Boot a fresh showcase and sign the admin in through the form.
2. Make an app in a writable package the current default. Here that was `mthree_app` in `com.objectstack.qa.mthree`, published with `isDefault:true`.
3. Open `/_console/system/apps` and click "Set Showcase as default" on the Showcase row (package `com.example.showcase`).
4. The page sends two writes in this order:
   - `PUT /api/v1/meta/app/mthree_app?package=com.objectstack.qa.mthree` with `isDefault:false` → **200**.
   - `PUT /api/v1/meta/app/showcase_app?package=com.example.showcase` with `isDefault:true` → **403** "Cannot overlay 'app' in package 'com.example.showcase': that package is read-only…".
5. A toast says "Failed to set default app: …".
6. After a reload, `GET /api/v1/meta/app` has no item with `isDefault:true` (before: `["mthree_app"]`), and the next sign-in lands on `/_console/home`.
- Expected: a refused set-default leaves `/meta/app` unchanged.
- Actual: the previous default is cleared and stays cleared.

**identity-auth.sso-enforced-first-paint · rev 4 · acceptance[3] · fail.** Reproduced twice.
1. Boot with `OS_SSO_ENABLED=true OS_AUTH_SSO_ONLY=true`.
2. Register one OIDC provider (`qa-fixture oidc-stub` plus `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/register`).
3. Open `/_console/login` in a fresh browser. Make `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/sso` never answer (a Playwright `page.route` that never fulfils).
4. Type an email and click "Sign in with SSO".
- Expected: after about 20 s the sign-in watchdog (#2626) recovers the button with an error and a retry path.
- Actual: at 22 s and at 32 s the button is still spinning and the email field is still disabled.
